title: Hallucination-Free? Assessing the Reliability of Leading AI Legal Research Tools
authors_or_organization: Varun Magesh, Faiz Surani, Matthew Dahl, Mirac Suzgun, Christopher D. Manning, Daniel E. Ho (Stanford RegLab/HAI; Yale)
publication_date: 2024-05-30 (arXiv v1); published version: Journal of Empirical Legal Studies 22(2):216-242, 2025, doi:10.1111/jels.12413
data_collection_dates: Lexis+ AI, Ask Practical Law AI, GPT-4 queries run 2024-03-22 to 2024-04-22; Westlaw AI-Assisted Research run 2024-05-23 to 2024-05-27 (per arXiv v1 Section 5)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Academic study of commercial products from LexisNexis and Thomson Reuters; funding not extracted.
limitations: Full text read is arXiv v1 (2024-05-30). The published JELS 2025 version could not be downloaded (connection reset) and figures may differ slightly; v1 itself notes revalidation moved one accuracy figure from 19% to 20%. 202 preregistered queries; benchmark of tool outputs, not of lawyers' verification behavior; tools change over time.

title: AI-Powered Lawyering: AI Reasoning Models, Retrieval Augmented Generation, and the Future of Legal Practice
authors_or_organization: Daniel Schwarcz, Sam Manning, J.J. Prescott, Patrick Barry, David R. Cleveland, Beverly Rich
publication_date: 2026 (Journal of Law & Empirical Analysis, vol. 3, p. 220, per repository listing); SSRN working paper 5162111 (2025)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Not determined. The RAG tool studied (Vincent AI) is a commercial product (vLex, later Clio); relationship of authors to vendor not checked.
limitations: Full-text PDF (UMN repository) and SSRN page returned Cloudflare/403 blocks. Only the repository abstract (as summarized by a fetch tool, not verbatim) and secondary coverage were seen. Hallucination counts (Vincent 3, o1-preview 11, no-AI 4) come from a search-engine summary of Law360 coverage and are NOT verified against the paper. UMN Law magazine (Spring 2025) reported productivity gains of 34-140%, which differs from the abstract's ~50-130%; likely different paper versions or metrics. Participants were law students, not practicing lawyers.

title: ABA Formal Opinion 512: Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools
authors_or_organization: American Bar Association Standing Committee on Ethics and Professional Responsibility
limitations: Primary PDF blocked (Cloudflare challenge via curl; HTTP 403 via fetch tool). Text relied on is the verbatim block quotation reproduced in Matt Stephens, 'Competence and the Lawyer's Use of GenAI: ABA formal opinion 512' (josephhollander.com, 2024-08-31), corroborated by The Bar Examiner (NCBE, Fall 2024) and National Law Review (2026) quotations. Original page numbers not located. ABA formal opinions are advisory, not binding; they state an obligation, not compliance.

title: The American Bar Association and Mississippi Bar Are Giving Lawyers Flawed AI Guidance
authors_or_organization: Oliver Roberts (National Law Review, AI & the Law Newsletter)
limitations: Opinion/commentary; no new data. Represents one commentator's normative position.

title: Da Silva Moore v. Publicis Groupe & MSL Group, Opinion and Order, No. 11 Civ. 1279 (ALC)(AJP), 287 F.R.D. 182 (S.D.N.Y. Feb. 24, 2012) (Peck, M.J.)
authors_or_organization: U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York (Magistrate Judge Andrew J. Peck)
limitations: Approval was based partly on the parties' agreement and on a specific protocol; the court said the protocol would not necessarily suit all cases. Affirmed by District Judge Carter (Apr. 26, 2012) - affirmance not read. Shows judicial acceptance, not measured outcomes in this case.

title: Rio Tinto PLC v. Vale S.A., Opinion and Order, No. 14 Civ. 3042 (RMB)(AJP), 306 F.R.D. 125 (S.D.N.Y. Mar. 3, 2015) (Peck, M.J.), with attached stipulated TAR protocol
authors_or_organization: U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York (Magistrate Judge Andrew J. Peck)
limitations: Copy hosted by a law firm (Steptoe) - ECF-stamped Document 207, 17 pages. Court approved a stipulated protocol and expressly did not rule on seed-set transparency. Statements on alternative validation means are dicta.

title: Technology-Assisted Review in E-Discovery Can Be More Effective and More Efficient Than Exhaustive Manual Review
authors_or_organization: Maura R. Grossman, Gordon V. Cormack
data_collection_dates: TREC 2009 Legal Track Interactive Task data
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Grossman was a TREC Legal Track coordinator and counsel at Wachtell Lipton; Cormack led the Waterloo team whose results are among those analyzed; H5 is a commercial vendor. Potential interest in the result.
limitations: Secondary analysis of TREC 2009 data; compares the two best-performing TAR efforts (5 topic-runs) with TREC assessor manual review, not a random sample of TAR systems; gold standard derived via adjudication of appealed documents; law-student and contract-reviewer assessors; law-review venue (student-edited, not peer-reviewed in the scientific sense).

title: The Sedona Conference TAR Case Law Primer, Second Edition (Public Comment Version)
authors_or_organization: The Sedona Conference Working Group 1 (Electronic Document Retention and Production)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Sedona Conference is a nonprofit; working group members include practitioners and vendors.
limitations: Public-comment version marked as superseded by a final edition (not read). It is a secondary summary of court decisions; the underlying decisions (Diisocyanates, Lawson, Domestic Airline, City of Rockford) were not read directly.

title: Mata v. Avianca, Inc., Opinion and Order on Sanctions, No. 22-cv-1461 (PKC), 678 F. Supp. 3d 443 (S.D.N.Y. June 22, 2023)
authors_or_organization: U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York (Judge P. Kevin Castel)
limitations: Single, extreme case (bad faith found partly because counsel stood by fake cases after being challenged). Shows legal standard and consequences, not typical verification practice.

title: AI Hallucination Cases Database
data_collection_dates: Decisions from Q2 2023 to access date
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Compiler has developed a commercial-adjacent automated reference checker ('PelAIkan') per the page.
limitations: Only the landing page and its filter counts were read; individual entries not audited. Compiler-curated (inclusion is a 'judgment call'); covers only decisions addressing hallucinations, not the universe of AI-assisted filings, so no rate/denominator. Counts change over time.

title: CG 300 Technical approval of highway structures (formerly BD 2/12), Version 0.2.1, Design Manual for Roads and Bridges
authors_or_organization: National Highways and UK Overseeing Organisations (DMRB)
limitations: Standard shows obligation, not compliance, cost, or effectiveness. Clause numbering in the extracted text is partly scrambled by PDF layout; clauses 2.69-2.75 pinned, the category list clause number not pinned.

title: 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix B - Quality Assurance Criteria for Nuclear Power Plants and Fuel Reprocessing Plants (Criteria III Design Control and VII Control of Purchased Material, Equipment, and Services)
limitations: Regulation states obligations; implementing standards (e.g., ASME NQA-1) and inspection findings not reviewed. Nuclear safety context has extreme consequence profile.

title: Guidelines for Performance-Based Seismic Design of Tall Buildings, Version 2.03 (PEER Report 2017/06)
authors_or_organization: Pacific Earthquake Engineering Research Center (PEER), Tall Buildings Initiative working group (co-chairs R. Hamburger, J. Moehle)
limitations: Consensus guideline/commentary; statements about review efficiency are expert judgment, not measured outcomes.

title: Expectations, Outcomes, and Challenges of Modern Code Review
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Conducted at Microsoft (second author Microsoft Research employee).
limitations: Exploratory mixed-methods field study (observation/interviews with 17 developers, 570 review comments, surveys of 165 managers and 873 programmers) at one company; not an experiment; self-reported survey answers. source_type closest available label; actually an observational field study.

title: Modern Code Review: A Case Study at Google
authors_or_organization: Caitlin Sadowski, Emma Soderberg, Luke Church, Michal Sipko, Alberto Bacchelli
data_collection_dates: Review logs covering ~9 million reviewed changes over two years (dates not extracted)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Most authors Google employees at the time.
limitations: Descriptive case study (12 interviews, survey of 44, log analysis) at one company; no causal identification of what makes review lightweight; does not measure defect escape. source_type closest available label; actually an observational case study.
